results.fact: Approach line (Easy Ridge vs Whatcom Pass/Brush Creek)
results.evidence: Real: the itinerary and PUBLISHED TIMES reproduce a documented 4-day Easy Ridge-in / Whatcom Pass-out loop that climbs the peak from Perfect Pass and only crosses the Whatcom Glacier on day 3, while the approach, variant, waypoints and climbing route ascend from Whatcom Pass across the glacier. Both lines are real, but making the itinerary match the Whatcom Pass ascent would need a whole new sourced day-by-day plan (miles, gain, hours) that no source provides for this line, so no patch.

results.fact: Chilliwack River crossing (ford vs cable car)

Easy Ridge accounts ford the river just below the old climbers' trail (thigh- to calf-deep). So the approach is right for its line, and the ford hazard, gear and waypoint belong to the Easy Ridge approach; they are now labelled that way.

results.fact: Gain vs loss on a loop that ends at the trailhead
results.evidence: A detailed account of exactly this 4-day loop gives 13,700 ft gained and lost; a speed-record route page gives 12,000 ft of gain for the 37-mile trip. The two do not agree, so gain_ft/loss_ft are left unchanged.

South-side ascents are documented in late July and in early and mid August (one mid-August car-to-car record), while a late-August party was turned back by bare ice and a wide moat. No source settles a month-by-month rating or whether September belongs in the working window, so nothing is changed.

The approach's 800 ft is measured from the Impasse notch (~5,200 ft) down to ~4,400 ft, as one detailed account gives; the bivy note's 'roughly 1,000 ft' is a round figure other accounts also use, and the bypass line varies with snow. Both are approximations of the same detour, and bivy[] is out of scope.
